doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Was he stereotyped as a jazz writer in the studios?
summary: He says no more than a white jazz writer would be.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: As a writer, composer, and arranger, did you find yourself, in coming out of the world of jazz and being a black composer, did you find yourself stereotyped in the studios? Did they come to you primarily thinking, you know, “We need some jazz here. We’ll get Benny Carter to do this,” as opposed to coming to you and saying, “We just need some kind of non-jazz-related music, and we’ll go to you as well.” Was there this stereotyping at the beginning?

I don’t think any more so than it would have been with a white musician that wrote so-called jazz. No, I don’t think so. I’d rather not think that I was hired because I was black, you know, in any instance.
